title: Restriction of the completion unit to strata and covering slices
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ an ideal. On the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], set $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/I^n}_T$, using constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves, their derived categories, and local derived ideal completeness [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. For a locally closed immersion $i:S\to X$, the canonical finite-projection comparison $i^{-1}B_X\to B_S$, with $i^{-1}$ the pro-étale inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], is an isomorphism. Restriction further to an object $U$ of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ means restriction to the slice site [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Under these identifications, restriction carries the actual Koszul completion unit of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] for $M\in D(B_X)$ to the corresponding unit for $M|_S$ and for $M|_U$. It also commutes with the canonical derived finite reductions $M\otimes^L_{B_X}\underline{A/I^n}_X$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. In particular local derived $IB_X$-completeness restricts along these functors. If $X=\coprod_\alpha S_\alpha$ is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] and a pro-étale covering is chosen on each stratum, then $M$ is locally derived complete if and only if all these restrictions are locally derived complete.

proof.text: Lift preservation of inverse sequences from the underlying sets to ring sheaves by the ringUnderlying natural isomorphism and reflection of limits. The constants isomorphism gives an isomorphism of the finite quotient diagrams. Its postcomposed image limit cone is limiting, and its unique map to the target limit is exactly completedMap, projection by projection. For immersion inverse images use the existing all-limit preservation theorem; slice set restriction preserves limits sectionwise. Thus both canonical coefficient maps are isomorphisms. The module adjunction and coefficient isomorphism make pullback exact; its left derived comparison is invertible on every complex.

Transport exact countable products from the original pro-etale module categories to small site models, and to covering slices through the post-equivalence of over categories and weakly-etale slice equivalence. Apply exactCompletedKoszulPullback to both immersion and slice inverse images. It gives a natural completion comparison carrying the actual Koszul unit to the corresponding unit.

The already normalized completedFinitePull comparison gives the finite-reduction equation. Expand the definition of finiteComparison, cancel the inverse pair finiteDerivedComparison.hom and .inv under the finite pullback, and reassociate; the required equation is its choose_spec normalization.

For an arbitrary supplied Koszul presentation compare it and the reflector presentation to the same augmented Cech completion via exists_ringed_cech_koszul_hom_limit_comparison. The normalized unit equations identify its unit with the reflector unit up to isomorphism. Hence invertibility of any supplied Koszul unit is equivalent to local derived completeness. The preceding transport equation then proves preservation.

Forward detection is successive preservation under stratum and slice pullback. Conversely choose a global presentation and presentations on strata and slices. The two actual unit equations show that each composite restriction sends the global unit to an isomorphism whenever that local object is complete. Apply adicStratumCoverConservativity to the global unit and then its unit criterion. This retains the unbounded completion and finite-stratum argument of the unit route.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2), Remark 6.5.10 and Proposition 6.6.11 reverse implication, with explicit ring limit comparison and finite-reduction cancellation; two general transport lemmas retain steps 3-5 of the original plan.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q135-7944355cf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all five steps, the statement of every cited node, the unit sk-lem-integral-models, and the Bhatt–Scholze sources: Lemma 6.5.8(1)–(2) with its proof (k^* commutes with limits), Remark 6.5.10, and the reverse direction of Proposition 6.6.11. The retained statement is a faithful generalization: any Noetherian A, any finitely generated I, any locally closed immersion, and local derived completeness, which equals Koszul-unit invertibility by lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence. There are no new nodes and no SGA source. Step checks: (1) Immersion limit preservation, which holds for every locally closed immersion with no Noetherian hypothesis, plus the scalar-identity constant-sheaf comparison, gives the isomorphism i^{-1}B_X ≅ B_S projection by projection. The isomorphism clause gives exactness and limit preservation of F_i. (2) Slice restriction is exact with the left adjoint j_!, and the weakly-étale localization identifies B_S|_U with B_U. (3) Tensor pullback plus K-flat preservation. Because Q_m is finite free, the Koszul tower, its transitions (a_j in degree −1, identity in degree 0) and the augmentations γ_m carry over termwise; I checked r=1 by hand. (4) Exact countable products for any pro-étale ring sheaf. The normalized strict Roos statement identifies the augmentation (γ_m, 0) with the derived augmentation, and the additive Roos comparison carries it to (Fγ_m, 0), so Fη_M = η_{FM}. (5) The detection lemma's hypotheses match: Noetherian X, a finite stratification, arbitrary chosen covers and an arbitrary ring sheaf, in the unbounded derived category. Edge cases tested: empty X or empty strata, I=0 or r=0, I=A, repeated generators, A/I^n of infinite projective dimension, and unbounded M. Fault (C1/C4), repaired: steps 3 and 5 apply the morphism-of-topoi tensor-pullback lemma and the stratum-detection lemma, both stated with r^{-1} of def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, to slice restriction, with no node identifying the two. I added the existing node lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction (r^{-1}G ≅ G|_W for sets, abelian groups and rings) to steps 2 and 5 with explicit sentences, recomputed proof_deps, and added a tool_use entry. The 11 declared tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes.
